_about: WHAT EACH SCHOOL SAYS IT WANTS ON A HIGH-SCHOOL TRANSCRIPT, from its own
admissions site. A FIFTH evidence source, and the most concrete one we hold.
corpus ............... what an admit looked like            (our CSV)
admit_rates .......... how selective the school is          (published rates)
college_weights ...... what the school says it WEIGHS       (CDS C7)
THIS FILE ............ what the school says to TAKE         (admissions site)
C7 says rigour is Very Important; it does not say which courses. This file does,
and unlike C7 it is published in plain HTML by every school, so the five of six
blocked for CDS are readable here.
THE DISTINCTION THAT MATTERS ON THE PAGE: 'required' means an application is
incomplete without it. 'recommended' means the school says it helps. 'expected'
is a school describing its admitted students rather than setting a bar. Never
print one as another - telling a family a recommendation is a requirement is the
same failure as over-goaling, in the one place a parent cannot check us.
NEVER state a figure this file does not hold. Penn publishes NO year counts at
all - it says to take core subjects for four years and names calculus for
Wharton. A filled-in guess for Penn would look exactly like the rest of this
file and be a fabrication. [see college_weights.json's UCLA near-miss]
_refresh: Admissions sites change with each cycle. Re-verify anything older than 12 months.

Michigan.framing: expects; varies by college within the university

english.note: with at least two rigorous writing courses

mathematics.note: varies by school within the university

science.note: at least two laboratory science courses

Michigan.overall: Five units (full-year courses) during each of the four years.
Michigan.rigour: Elect AP, IB, honors, enriched and accelerated courses when appropriate and available.

McDonough School of Business.mathematics: Minimum three years of math, through advanced algebra and trigonometry. Calculus is required within the program.
McDonough School of Business.science: Two years of natural science are recommended.

Penn.general: Take classes in core academic areas - English, social studies, math, science and foreign language - throughout your four years of high school.

by_school.Wharton: Strong preparation in mathematics, including calculus.
by_school.Engineering: Strong preparation in physics and mathematics, particularly calculus.
by_school.Nursing: Strong preparation in the sciences, particularly chemistry and biology.

Penn.caution: Penn states no year counts. Do not supply any.

NYU.framing: describes best-prepared students; explicitly NOT a bar

by_school.Stern School of Business: Should have calculus or, at least, precalculus on their transcript.

NYU.caveat: NYU states it will not hold students at a disadvantage if they did not have the option.

_uc_a_g.framing: REQUIRED - this is a hard gate, not a recommendation

a_history.note: one year world history/cultures/historical geography, plus one year US history (or half US history and half civics/American government)

c_mathematics.note: a fourth year of math is strongly recommended

e_world_language.note: the SAME language, or equivalent to the second level of high-school instruction

f_arts.note: one YEARLONG course in dance, music, theater, visual arts or interdisciplinary arts

_uc_a_g.course_list_caveat: A-G credit depends on the specific course appearing on that high school's UC-approved course list. A subject taken is not automatically a subject counted - the family must check their own school's list.
